newsitem.title: MEXICO: Four executed in Mexico City drug hit.
newsitem.headline: Four executed in Mexico City drug hit.

text.p: Drug hitmen gunned down a carload of rivals in downtown Mexico City on Thursday, killing four people and wounding one in the latest sign of rising drug violence in Mexico, police said.
"It most certainly was some kind of vendetta or vengeance by drug traffickers," Mexico City Judicial Police Chief Gen. Luis Roberto Gutierrez Flores said at a news conference.

The brazen, early morning attack was highly unusual even for the crime-infested streets of Mexico City, Gutierrez said. Two unidentified suspects were arrested but the case was far from closed, he said.
The car was riddled with more than 20 bullets and the victims were each shot multiple times by at least one assault rifle and at least one semiautomatic pistol, police said.

Although police immediately called it drug-related, they stopped short of linking it to a recent wave of violence that has plagued cities like Guadalajara and Cuidad Juarez, which are hubs for international drug traffickers.
This attack was among "low level" dealers, Gutierrez said.
"If you're talking about international drug traffickers, there definitely are links, but in this case we're talking about vendettas for control of a certain market," he said.

Three victims died on the spot and one bled to death on the way to a clinic. The survivor, Jessica Maribel Castillo Carbajal, the only woman in the car, made it to the clinic with the help of bystanders and gave a statement to police.

All the victims were unarmed and in their 30s, Gutierrez said. The dead were identified as Mario Luna Veladez, alias "El Capo," Javier Cadeno, also known as "El Brutus," Jose Margarito Quintero Sanchez and Fernando Gaspar Flores.
